findings.title: Unstable Python hash() used for shared cache key
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py the cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(...))). Python's hash() is salted per-process, so the same project list maps to different keys in different workers/restarts, and invalidate_upsampling_cache() computed in another process will delete a different key. Consequence: the 60s cache never shares across processes and invalidation does not work cross-process, defeating the optimization and leaving stale eligibility.

findings.title: upsampled_count uses bare sum(sample_weight) with no null fallback
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)). Events without a sample_weight (older events, non-sampled ingestion, transactions mixed in discover) have NULL/missing values which sum ignores or turns to NULL/0. Consequence: upsampled counts silently undercount instead of counting such rows as 1, producing wrong chart numbers. It needs coalesce/ifNotFinite handling, not an assumption that the column always exists.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py _get_event_stats() calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request) with the outer closure dataset, not the scoped_dataset argument it is about to query. The dashboard-split factory calls the same helper with discover vs metrics datasets to split errors/transactions. Consequence: split queries get the wrong upsampling decision, e.g. a discover errors-only split query evaluated against a metrics dataset will skip upsampling, or vice versa, returning inconsistent counts.

findings.title: Discover errors-only queries via negation never upsampled
findings.body: In src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py _is_error_focused_query() only returns True for the literal substring event.type:error. The endpoint itself builds errors-only discover queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction, and users commonly filter errors by exclusion. Consequence: those errors-only discover queries return False and use plain count() while explicit event.type:error queries use upsampled_count(), so the same logical data shows different numbers depending on query spelling.

findings.title: upsampled_count only registered on discover but applied to errors dataset
findings.body: In src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py the new SnQLFunction upsampled_count is added to the discover dataset converter, but src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py returns True for the errors dataset unconditionally and organization_events_stats.py rewrites count() to upsampled_count() for scoped_dataset==errors and for RPC paths. Consequence: errors-dataset timeseries/top-events and RPC queries will request an unknown function and fail or behave inconsistently because the function is not registered there.

findings.title: Test helper blindly overwrites sample_rate from error_sampling context
findings.body: In src/sentry/testutils/factories.py _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling() does normalized_data.get(contexts,{}).get(...) inside a bare except, checks if client_sample_rate: (skipping 0), then float()s anything and overwrites normalized_data[sample_rate] without validating range or preserving an existing explicit sample_rate. Consequence: invalid rates like 2.0, negative, or strings pollute stored events in tests, and real sample_rate values are silently replaced, making upsampling tests unrealistic and masking production null-handling bugs.
